affected_docs.why: Every one of its four sections is stated by a page that survives: requirements by installing.md lines 35-56, the house-and-window framing by _index.md lines 57-61, the three beats by first-run.md lines 22-30, the routing lists by _index.md lines 29-67, and the pre-alpha caveat by _index.md lines 19-20. claims.claim: The persona interview is a one-time event: once a persona is created, the first-run flow can never be entered again by ordinary use.
claims.evidence: backend/harness/valar/gateway/first_run.py:253-287. active() returns True only when every non-internal persona in the directory carries "shipped": true; the module docstring at lines 3-7 states that create_persona writing a new resident makes the next turn's detection fail. The only override is the HEARTH_FORCE_FIRST_RUN debug environment variable at lines 280-281, which the docstring says puts the whole house into interview mode.

claims.claim: A persona can still be created after first run, through the create_persona tool.
claims.evidence: backend/harness/valar/tools/handlers/creation.py:288-340 has no first-run gate: it validates the name, fills a missing description or system prompt from the other, and rejects only a case-insensitive name collision. backend/harness/valar/tools/tools.yaml:1083-1091 registers it in domain personas.

claims.claim: Only Sulivan can create a further persona; a persona made during first run cannot.
claims.evidence: backend/personas/Sulivan/sulivan.json:61-75 grants Sulivan the personas domain. backend/harness/valar/data/persona_template.json:31-36, the template every made persona is expanded from, grants domains weather, timers, search, news, memory, media, and personas is not among them. create_persona is the only tool in the personas domain (single match for "domain: personas" in tools.yaml).

claims.claim: A reader can reach Sulivan again after first run by clicking his chip on the persona stage.
claims.evidence: desktop-client/src/components/stage/PersonaChips.tsx:14-33 renders one button per persona and calls onSwitch with the name; desktop-client/src/components/stage/PersonaStage.tsx:59 renders the chips. backend/personas/Sulivan/sulivan.json:6 marks him shipped and the manifest sets neither internal nor desktop_only, so backend/harness/valar/persona/engine.py:80-82 does not hide him from the picker.

claims.claim: No published page tells a reader how to create a second persona.
claims.evidence: wiki/features/personas.md:46-71 describes only the first-run interview, opening "The first time you open Hearth". wiki/features/personas.md:104-113 states that switching by name works but names no route to creation. wiki/first-run.md:208-292 describes the interview as beat two of setup. Grep for create_persona across wiki/ excluding raw/ returns no reader-facing instruction.

claims.claim: wiki/features/personas.md is correct that a settings screen for editing or removing a persona is not yet covered by what ships today.
claims.evidence: wiki/features/personas.md:110-113 makes the claim. desktop-client/src/components/personas/PersonasView.tsx:102 defines a full persona settings view, reachable as a top-level view at desktop-client/src/App.tsx:232-235; it posts to /personas/apply (backend/harness/valar/gateway/personas_api.py:460-462), and backend/harness/valar/gateway/personas_api.py:336-375 applies per-persona edits and removes a persona by renaming its folder. Remove is gated behind developer mode at PersonasView.tsx:676-684, so the removing half is behind a flag rather than absent.

claims.claim: On an 8 GB machine Hearth warns that the persona will think and speak one at a time.
claims.evidence: wiki/installing.md:75-78 and wiki/first-run.md:182-186 both state it. crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:126-149 emits that warning only in the branch where nothing fits with the voice held resident. crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:338-344 asserts an 8 GB Air keeps its Q4_K_M quant and coexists, and crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:36-52 asserts p.coexist and that no warning containing "one at a time" is produced, with a comment saying the assertion used to be the opposite and omnivoice.cpp is what changed it. wiki/installing.md:40-42 states the correct version on the same page, so installing.md contradicts itself.

claims.claim: The default install root on Windows is D:\Hearth.
claims.evidence: wiki/installing.md:85-86, wiki/clients/windows.md:151 and wiki/first-run.md:112 all state it. crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:232-247 joins "Hearth" to the roomiest non-removable, non-system fixed drive, whichever letter that is, and falls back to %USERPROFILE%\.hearth, a hidden dotdir, on a single-drive machine. wiki/first-run.md:161-166 states the roomiest-drive rule correctly, so first-run.md contradicts itself, and no published page mentions the .hearth fallback.

claims.claim: The default install root on macOS is a visible folder named Hearth in the home directory.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:238-243, with the comment that it is visible on macOS because deleting the folder is the uninstall and a dotdir hides the thing a person owns.

claims.claim: A 16 GB machine plans Gemma 4 12B at a 65,536-token context window for a 7.14 GB download.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:198-211 gives tier 2 as Gemma 4 12B, file bytes 6716356800, max_ctx 65536; crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:112 gives the voice download as 945284608 bytes. crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:214-234 sums exactly those two into total_download_bytes: 7661641408 bytes, which is 7.14 GiB. crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:19 states that with these numbers a 16 GB card plans 65536 tokens.

claims.claim: An 8 GB Mac plans Gemma 4 E2B Q4_K_M for a 3.77 GB download.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:132-139 gives tier 0 as Gemma 4 E2B, file gemma-4-E2B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf at 3106738272 bytes; plus the voice at 945284608 (dictionary.yaml:112) sums to 4052022880 bytes, which is 3.77 GiB. crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:338-341 asserts the 8 GB Air lands on tier 0 at Q4_K_M. Note that the pages write GB where the value is GiB.

claims.claim: An 8 GB Mac gets a 17,408-token context window.
claims.evidence: Stated at wiki/installing.md:72 and wiki/install-macos.md:75. crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:280-283 derives the window from the remaining budget and rounds down to a multiple of 1024, and 17408 is 17 times 1024, so the value is the right shape. No fixture asserts it: crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:82 and crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:343 assert only that it clears the 16384 target. Settling it needs the planner run against the m1-air-8gb fixture, which is outside a read-only pass.

claims.claim: The five local programs and their ports, as listed on both client pages, are correct.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/src/defaults.rs:18-22 defines PORT_GATEWAY 18700, PORT_LLAMA 18080, PORT_SUPERVISOR_WS 18765, PORT_SUPERVISOR_ASSETS 18766, PORT_TTS 18702; backend/scripts/render_config.py:48-52 writes the same five. wiki/clients/macos.md:72-80 and wiki/clients/windows.md:170-176 both match.

claims.claim: The plan's download figure counts the model weights, the voice, the inference engine, and the Python runtime.
claims.evidence: wiki/installing.md:95-97 and wiki/install-macos.md:84-86 both list four things downloading. crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:214-234 builds the downloads vector from exactly two entries, the model build and the voice, and total_download_bytes sums only those. The dictionary comment at crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:110 says the engine binary ships in the bundle and only weights are fetched. The four things may all be provisioned; only two are in the number the plan shows.

claims.claim: Three published pages announce a Windows install guide that has never been written.
claims.evidence: wiki/installing.md:135-138, wiki/clients/macos.md:122, and wiki/clients/windows.md:232-234. A fourth mention, wiki/whats-not-here.md:23, is the landing page whose declared job is naming unwritten pages, so it is the one correct home rather than a fourth announcement.

claims.claim: wiki/installing.md carries platform subsections under ## Before you start.
claims.evidence: wiki/installing.md:35 (### macOS) and wiki/installing.md:48 (### Windows), both under ## Before you start at line 29.

claims.claim: No published page tells a reader where to obtain the Hearth installer.
claims.evidence: wiki/installing.md:24 opens "You have the Hearth installer" and treats it as given. wiki/getting-started.md:49-52 says the client is the installer and links onward without naming a source. wiki/releasing.md:40 names the artifact filename for someone cutting a release, not downloading one. wiki/updates.md:79 says a person gets a new app by downloading a .dmg without saying from where. A case-insensitive grep across wiki/ excluding raw/ for release links, .dmg, and download phrasing returns no reader-facing download location.

claims.claim: wiki/clients/macos.md carries an install procedure that page-types.md forbids on a platform overview.
claims.evidence: wiki/clients/macos.md:86-102 is a four-step numbered install procedure under ## Installing. wiki/page-types.md:241-244 states that installation lives on the install page, not on a platform overview, and that a platform overview which grows an install procedure has become a second install guide, "which is how the corpus ended up with two".

claims.claim: wiki/installing.md meets the how-to spine its declared type requires.
claims.evidence: wiki/page-types.md:108-116 requires action-title sections with numbered steps inside them, one action per step, imperative mood. wiki/installing.md contains no numbered list and no imperative step from line 22 to line 147; its sections are narrative descriptions of what the installer does, and its own abstract at line 26-27 calls it "the narrative version of the install".

claims.claim: wiki/first-run.md is a how-to, as its frontmatter declares.
claims.evidence: wiki/first-run.md:4 declares type: how-to. The page's content is a design record: dated decisions at lines 52, 87, 105 and 159, rules derived from a bug at lines 62-85, tool parameter schemas at lines 258-286, an unresolved implementation note at lines 288-292, and a four-item ## Open questions section at lines 322-333. wiki/page-types.md:156-181 describes exactly this shape as a decision record, and wiki/page-types.md:150-154 states that a concept or record page containing steps belongs on a how-to page it links to. Its frontmatter sources at lines 10-11 are two unpublished research documents.

gaps: No page states where to download Hearth, so the install journey has no first step.
No page states how to create a persona after first run, and no page states that only Sulivan can.
No page states that a persona made during first run cannot itself make another persona.
No Windows install procedure exists anywhere in the corpus; three pages announce it as missing.
No page describes the shipped persona settings screen (PersonasView), which edits every persona field and removes a persona in developer mode.
No page states the Windows single-drive fallback install root, %USERPROFILE%\.hearth, which is a hidden dotdir and sits awkwardly beside the one-folder uninstall story every install page tells.
No page states what the plan's download figure actually counts. Two pages imply it covers four items; the planner sums two.
There is no canonical source outside the repository for any of this, and none is needed: Hearth reaches no external service, so every behavioural claim here was settled in the tree.

breaks.why: The journey's first action has no page. wiki/installing.md:24 opens "You have the Hearth installer" and treats it as already true; wiki/getting-started.md:49-52 says the client is the installer without naming where it comes from. wiki/releasing.md:40 names the artifact for someone cutting a release, not downloading one. Nothing in the published corpus names a download location.

wiki/installing.md carries no numbered step for either platform, and its ### Windows subsection at lines 48-56 states requirements then hands off to a platform overview. The only complete procedure in the corpus is wiki/install-macos.md. wiki/installing.md:135-138 says the Windows guide does not exist, and wiki/clients/macos.md:122 and wiki/clients/windows.md:232-234 say it again. A Windows reader following the journey reaches step one and stops.

breaks.objective: read the plan Hearth shows you and approve it
breaks.why: The pages describe a plan the planner does not produce. wiki/installing.md:75-78 and wiki/first-run.md:182-186 tell an 8 GB reader to expect a warning that the persona will think and speak one at a time; crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:126-149 emits that only when nothing fits with the voice resident, and crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:36-52 asserts an 8 GB Air coexists and gets no such warning. wiki/installing.md:40-42 states the correct version forty lines earlier, so the same page tells the reader both.

breaks.objective: set the install root to a folder with room
breaks.why: wiki/installing.md:85-86, wiki/clients/windows.md:151 and wiki/first-run.md:112 all say the Windows default is D:\Hearth. crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:232-247 joins Hearth to whichever non-removable, non-system fixed drive has the most free space, and falls back to %USERPROFILE%\.hearth on a single-drive machine. A single-drive Windows reader is shown a hidden dotdir no page mentions, which quietly undercuts the one-folder uninstall story every install page tells.

breaks.objective: read the plan Hearth shows you and approve it
breaks.why: Five published pages teach it: wiki/installing.md:58-79, wiki/install-macos.md:56-94, wiki/clients/macos.md:86-102, wiki/clients/windows.md:188-207, and wiki/first-run.md:176-186. Two of them print the same plan table with different rows: wiki/install-macos.md:72-78 carries Backend and Mind-and-voice rows that wiki/installing.md:68-73 drops. A reader who reads two of the five gets two different answers about their own machine.

breaks.objective: create a persona after first run has ended
breaks.why: This is the break the journey's own name points at, and the corpus does not answer it. The route exists in the product: create_persona has no first-run gate (backend/harness/valar/tools/handlers/creation.py:288-340) and lives in the personas tool domain (backend/harness/valar/tools/tools.yaml:1083-1091), which Sulivan holds (backend/personas/Sulivan/sulivan.json:61-75) and which a made persona does not (backend/harness/valar/data/persona_template.json:31-36). So the answer is: switch back to Sulivan on the persona chips and ask him. Every page stops short of it. wiki/features/personas.md:46-71 is headed "Making your first one" and opens "The first time you open Hearth". wiki/first-run.md:208-292 describes the interview as beat two of setup. wiki/features/personas.md:104-113 says switching works, and then closes the door: "Beyond that, day-to-day details of managing several personas ... are not yet covered by what ships today."

breaks.objective: understand that the interview will not run twice
breaks.why: Nothing in the corpus states that the guided interview is one-shot, and the mechanism is not obvious. backend/harness/valar/gateway/first_run.py:253-287 makes first run active only while every non-internal persona is marked shipped, so the moment create_persona writes a resident the interview expires permanently. A reader who assumes they can repeat the flow they were just walked through is wrong, and no page tells them.

breaks.objective: edit or remove a persona you have made
breaks.why: wiki/features/personas.md:110-113 sends the reader away from a surface that ships. desktop-client/src/components/personas/PersonasView.tsx:102 is a full persona settings view reachable as a top-level view (desktop-client/src/App.tsx:232-235); it posts to /personas/apply (backend/harness/valar/gateway/personas_api.py:460-462), which applies edits and removes personas by renaming the folder (personas_api.py:336-375). Removing is behind developer mode (PersonasView.tsx:676-684); editing is not. The page is wrong about editing and imprecise about removing.

verdicts.why: The survivor, and the only page in the cluster already parameterized by platform: ### macOS at line 35 and ### Windows at line 48 under ## Before you start. It is the page wiki/_index.md:30 routes to and the page wiki/page-types.md:102 names as a how-to in the corpus. Keeping it is conditional on three repairs it needs whether or not anything folds into it: the abstract at line 24 must stop assuming the reader already holds the installer, the 8 GB claim at lines 75-78 must go (it contradicts both line 40-42 and crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:126-149), and the Windows install root at lines 85-86 must match crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:232-247. It also has no numbered step anywhere, which wiki/page-types.md:108-116 requires of its declared type; absorbing install-macos.md's procedure is what fixes that.

Its requirements, plan, download, and Sulivan-speaks sections are the same objectives installing.md already teaches, and the two pages print the same plan table with different rows. It is not a delete: four of its sections are taught nowhere else in the corpus, and one of them is the only numbered procedure in the whole cluster. Fold it into installing.md's ### macOS subsection with the salvage intact, then retire the page. wiki/_index.md:31, wiki/whats-not-here.md:23, wiki/updates.md:105, wiki/clients/macos.md:29,89,127 and wiki/clients/windows.md:233 all point at it and would need redirecting.

Four of its five sections are correct platform overview work: what the Mac needs, what installing gives you, updating, and the honest limits. The exception is ## Installing at lines 86-102, a fourth copy of the install procedure that wiki/page-types.md:241-244 explicitly forbids here, naming it as how the corpus ended up with two install guides in the first place. Remove that section, keep a link. Also retire the line 122 announcement of the missing Windows guide: an announcement belongs on wiki/whats-not-here.md:23 and nowhere else.

It is the only page documenting the Windows process tree, the session and memory and file-permission surfaces, and the Windows limits, and none of that is duplicated anywhere. Its overlap with installing.md is confined to ## What the installer gives you (lines 145-186) and ## The hardware probe picks your model (lines 188-207). Trim those to what is Windows-specific, and fix the D:\Hearth default at line 151. Separately, ## What the desktop app is runs lines 28-143 and is largely how-to and reference material inside a platform overview; that is a split worth its own task rather than part of this consolidation, and it does not change the keep verdict.

Every one of its four sections is taught by a page that survives: requirements by installing.md lines 35-56, the house-and-window framing by _index.md lines 57-61 (and clients/ios.md:23, clients/android.md:26), the three steps by first-run.md lines 22-30, the routing by _index.md lines 29-67, and the pre-alpha caveat by _index.md lines 19-20. It teaches no step of its own, and its declared type: how-to disagrees with what it does: it routes, which is a landing page, and _index.md is already that page. It is not a delete: it uniquely holds the reader's position before they have an installer, which installing.md's abstract explicitly rules out for itself. Fold the requirements paragraph into installing.md's ## Before you start, let _index.md keep the routing, and retire the page. wiki/_index.md:7,29 name it.

open_questions: Which page in the install cluster survives, and what must be salvaged from each page that does not? Answered: installing.md survives; install-macos.md and getting-started.md fold; both client pages keep with their install sections trimmed. The salvage list is complete above. What remains open is whether the author stage agrees that getting-started.md should retire at all, given it is the front door wiki/_index.md:29 names first.

Should installing.md and first-run.md both cover installation, or does one hand off to the other? Answered in one direction: installing.md hands off at its ## What comes next, line 121-126, and that seam is correct. The open half is what first-run.md becomes. It is declared how-to and is written as a decision record, so the handoff currently lands a reader in a design document with four unresolved open questions at lines 322-333. Does first-run.md get retyped to decision-record, with a new reader-facing first-run how-to written beside it, or does it get rewritten in place as the how-to it claims to be?

Can a reader who already finished first run create a second persona, and does any page tell them how? Answered: yes, and no. The route is to switch back to Sulivan and ask him, because he holds the personas tool domain and a made persona does not. No published page states it. What is open is whether that is the intended product route or an accident of the persona template's default grants, which is a product question this pass cannot settle from the tree.

Should a persona made during first run be able to make another persona? backend/harness/valar/data/persona_template.json:31-36 excludes the personas domain from a made persona's grants, with the comment "Resident defaults. No dev, no briefs; those are the operator's own surfaces." The comment does not say whether excluding persona creation was deliberate or incidental. The documentation cannot describe the route confidently until someone says.

Is the plan's download figure meant to cover four provisioned items or the two it sums? crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:214-234 sums the model build and the voice only, while wiki/installing.md:95-97 and wiki/install-macos.md:84-86 both describe four things downloading. Either the prose is overstating what the number covers, or the inference engine and Python runtime are fetched by a path outside the planner that this pass did not find.

What context window does an 8 GB Mac actually plan? Both install pages say 17,408 tokens. The value has the right shape (crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:280-283 rounds to a multiple of 1024) but no fixture asserts it, and confirming it needs the planner run rather than read.

Does the Windows single-drive fallback to %USERPROFILE%\.hearth need documenting, or fixing? A hidden dotdir contradicts the reasoning at crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:239-240, which says the folder is visible on macOS precisely because deleting it is the uninstall. That is a product question, not a documentation one, but the documentation cannot state the default correctly until it is answered.
